title: Genesis Primitives are single-use and structurally sealed once invoked, so an Agent's origin cannot be re-run
content:
Three of Keel's Genesis Primitives declare themselves exhausted. A.6.1.1.3.2.1.1.4 and A.6.1.1.3.2.1.1.1.4 state that "because the Agent Creation Primitive is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked." A.6.1.1.3.2.1.2.4 says the same for Prime Transformation, and A.6.1.1.3.2.1.4.4 for the Agent Token Primitive ("solely for the one-time deployment of the Agent's token").

What makes this architectural rather than incidental is that the directories are still *present*. Every Primitive Hub carries the same slots — Active Instances, Completed Instances, In Progress Invocations, Hub Data Repository — and a single-use Primitive fills the invocation slot with a statement of impossibility instead of deleting it. The shape of the tree is uniform across all Primitives; only the contents record that this one can never fire again.

The consequence is that an Agent's constitutional facts — that it exists, that it is a Prime Agent, that its token was deployed once — are not re-derivable by re-invoking a Primitive. Changing them requires editing the Artifact, not running a process. Origin events are made non-repeatable at the level of the document structure, which is a cheaper guarantee than any runtime access control.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation and Agent Token each state that no further Instances can be Invoked; the In Progress Invocations directory exists but is permanently closed by construction.
